title: Partisanship and political interest as moderators of the video effect
rationale: The Perception gap video lowered affective polarization by 2.3 points (p=0.019), but subgroup estimates by interest had opposing signs (high -1.502, SE 1.382; low +1.090, SE 0.912) and by party were similar (Dem -1.671, Rep -1.309), with no interaction test. This design tests the interactions with adequate power.
contribution: Provides a pre-registered, adequately powered test of whether the Perception gap video effect differs by party and political interest.
limitations: Interest and party measured by self-report; independents excluded
Single video; online panel may not be representative
Measuring interest pre-treatment could prime respondents

design.title: Partisanship and political interest as moderators of the Perception gap video effect
design.overview: US online-panel respondents who are Democrats or Republicans with high or low political interest are randomized to control or the Perception gap video, within party-by-interest strata. Affective polarization is measured before and after.
design.hypothesis: The video effect on post_ap differs by political interest (treatment x interest) and by party (treatment x party). Pre-registered as the primary two-sided interaction tests.
design.primaryOutcome: post_ap: in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer after treatment, adjusting for pre_ap.
design.comparison: Perception gap video vs control, with treatment-by-interest and treatment-by-party interaction terms, controlling for pre_ap.
design.population: US adults from an online panel, Democrats and Republicans (including leaners), with high interest (very or extremely interested) or low interest (not very or not at all interested). Somewhat interested respondents are screened out.

conditions.title: Control

conditions.title: Perception gap video
conditions.description: Watches the Perception gap video with misperception data.

questions.text: You are invited to take part in a research study on political attitudes. It takes about 10 minutes, is voluntary, and your answers are confidential. Do you consent to participate?
Do you think of yourself as closer to the Republican Party or to the Democratic Party?
Generally, how interested are you in politics?
Please rate each group on the feeling thermometer, from 0 (cold) to 100 (warm). Choose the point on the scale closest to your feeling.
What did you just see, read, or watch?
Please rate each group on the feeling thermometer, from 0 (cold) to 100 (warm). Choose the point on the scale closest to your feeling.
Thank you. This study examined how short videos affect views of political groups. The video presented survey data on how partisans perceive each other. Contact the research team with any questions.

flow.label: Video stimulus
flow.value: [VIDEO: Perception gap video showing how much partisans misperceive the other party, about 5 minutes]

assumptions: Power target: about 1600 per arm to detect a 2.5-point subgroup difference at 80% power, since the interaction SE is roughly double the main-effect SE (~1.0).
Randomization is pre-stratified by party x interest; quotas fill the four cells roughly equally, with the survey platform enforcing quotas.
Analysis: OLS with HC2 errors, pre_ap covariate, and interaction terms; high interest is >=4 and low is <=2.
Thermometer is collected as 5-point banded matrix because slider type is unavailable; a slider can be used on the platform.
unresolved: The Perception gap video file must be supplied and hosted by the research team.
